Description - Download

Resolves download entries to files, lists the agreements (transfer types) offered for each file, and, once an agreement is accepted, returns a signed url for GET /File.aspx.

Two steps (as the client does): (1) send entries without agreementInfo: each FileEntry lists the offered agreements and url is nil; (2) resend with the accepted agreement: url is filled. For own files the only offer is own/cost 0 (balance unchanged); paid agreements were never accepted live.

Agreements offered (live): exactly one per file in every case seen: own/0 for own files; small/0 for other users' files under 1 MB; transfer with cost = file size in kB, rounded down, above 1 MB (1654 for a 1,694,208-byte file). The foreign-file captures are read-only: nothing was accepted. free, edu, access and points were not observed. The 7 agreementInfo slots follow the client's type order: the offered name sits at its type's position (Observed: own in slot 1, small in 2, transfer in 6; Inferred for the others) and the other slots are nil. AgreementInfo lists every name the client knows and the cost units.

Outcomes by disposition: download works for any file. player.audio works like download for audio files (agreement offer first, then a signed url: mp3-audio-disposition-request, mp3-audio-disposition-own-agreement). For other files it returns Error / failed : requested file(s) not available with list and accountBalance nil (audio-disposition).

Forms: plain (token, disposition, list) or sequenced (with sequence{stamp, part, count}). The client uses the sequenced form and splits a request only above 2000 entries, so its normal requests are single messages (count 1). Ids: numeric file id; file path /<user>/<folder>/<file>; folder path /<user>/<folder> (returns all files of the folder, also for other users' folders: foreign-folder-listing-offers). .<realId> is accepted (status Ok) but has never been shown to resolve a file: realId was nil or 0 for every file seen (own uploads, playlist copies, other users' files), so only an unknown realId could be tried. The client builds .<realId> only for entries without a file id. The client's <hamsterId>/<folderId> form, built by its "download folder" action, triggers an unhandled server exception (a:InternalServiceFault), so that client feature presumably fails today (Inferred).

Sequenced Download: verified live with conditions (26 exchanges in four sessions, own files only):

  • A non-final part (part < count-1, a middle part included) is acknowledged with status Ok, list and accountBalance nil and messageSequence echoed. Its entries are stored server-side per session token: a second, concurrent session of the same account gets Error for the final part (seq1d-*).
  • The store is not keyed by the stamp and not cleared by a final part; a new part 0 replaces what was stored (seq1c-c4-final-d, seq1c-c5-final-alone-c, sequence-final-part-without-part0).
  • A final part returns the stored entries plus its own, resolved and grouped as usual, only if they are all in one folder; it does not expand the folder (sequence-final-part1-of-2, seq1c-c2-final-d, seq1c-c4-final-d).
  • If the combined entries span two folders, the reply is Ok with an empty <a:list/> (balance present): nothing is returned, not even the final part's own entry, and a stale stored part from another folder also empties a later final part (sequence-final-after-part0-other-folder, sequence-count3-final-part2, sequence-final-part-alone-own-agreement).
  • A final part with nothing stored in the session gives status Error with a nil errorMessage and nil list (three sessions: sequence-final-part-alone-fresh-session, seq1c-c0-final-alone-fresh-session, seq1d-session2-final-d-same-stamp).
  • Agreements count only in the final message: with own in the final part both entries got a url; with own only in part 0 neither did (sequence-own-agreement-final-part1-of-2, seq1c-c9-final-d-no-agreement). Whether a final-message agreement applies per entry or per type: Unknown.
  • A count-1 message ignores stored parts (single-message-after-sequences). The balance was unchanged throughout.

Consequences (Inferred): a client request of more than 2000 files from more than one folder would come back empty, and two sequenced requests running in one session (downloader and player) could mix their parts (S-13).

When the client sends it: downloader and player; :resentTimeout = message-download-resent-timeout (45 s). Download results that contain files set a guid tracking cookie.

Routing. The path item declares the server http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=, so this operation resolves to http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=/Download. WCF ignores the query string and dispatches only on the SOAPAction header (verified live). The real client posts to the bare http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc; both URLs reach the same operation. A path suffix (.svc/Download) does not work (a:DestinationUnreachable, see soapRestStylePath).

Wire format. POST with Content-Type: text/xml;charset=utf-8 (exact client bytes, no space; the server answers text/xml; charset=utf-8) and SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/Download (unquoted). Body: SOAP 1.1 envelope, UTF-8, no indentation, parameters in the documented order (WCF silently drops out-of-order parameters). The client gzips the body (Content-Encoding: gzip).

Path notes

SOAP operation Download. The path-level server makes the URL routable: WCF dispatches on SOAPAction and ignores the ?op=/Download query.

Request - body and examples

Body required.

SOAP 1.1 request envelope for Download (media type text/xml, charset UTF-8).

Body text/xml

Schema

Schema DownloadRequestEnvelope, as an XML element tree in wire order. Namespaces are shown where they change.

  • <s:Envelope> object required DownloadRequestEnvelope xmlns http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

    SOAP 1.1 request envelope for Download: <s:Envelope><s:Body><Download xmlns="http://chomikuj.pl/">…. No SOAP header is ever sent; xmlns:i is declared on the operation element only when a nil value is present.

    • @s:encodingStyle string optional = "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/encoding/" namespace http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

      SOAP 1.1 encodingStyle attribute. The real client always writes it; the service accepts the envelope with or without it.

    • <s:Body> object required

      Exactly one operation element; no other content (this also makes the per-operation envelopes mutually exclusive).

      • <Download> object required DownloadRequest xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

        Operation element Download in http://chomikuj.pl/ (trailing slash is mandatory: with http://chomikuj.pl the parameters are not matched, see Service/wrong-operation-namespace).

        • <token> string required Token

          Session token. Always the first child.

        • <sequence> object optional nullable (i:nil) MessageSequence

          Chunk header; sent when [network] sequence-soap=true (default config). Optional for the server; without it messageSequence is nil in the result.

          • <stamp> string required

            Random correlation value, the same for all parts (a random number generated by the client). The server does not key stored parts by it.

          • <part> integer (int32) required

            Zero-based part index.

          • <count> integer (int32) required

            Total number of parts.

        • <disposition> string required Disposition

          download (downloader) or player.audio (player).

        • <list> list required

          Requested entries.

          • <DownloadReqEntry> object optional repeated DownloadReqEntry

            One entry of a Download request.

            • <id> string required

              What to download. Forms built by the client, in order of precedence: <fileId> (the normal case); .<realId> only for an entry without a file id (accepted with status Ok, but realId was never non-zero live, so it has never been shown to resolve a file: Download/id-dot-realid); <hamsterId>/<folderId> for the client's "download folder" action (unhandled server exception: Download/id-hamster-slash-folder); a folder path or an external URL; empty. The service also accepts paths: /<user>/<folder>/<file> and /<user>/<folder>; the latter returns the folder with all its files, own or another user's (Download/folder-listing, Download/foreign-folder-listing-offers).

            • <agreementInfo> list optional

              Agreements accepted for this entry (present only when the user accepted one). Without it the response lists the offered agreements and url is nil.

              • <AgreementInfo> object optional nullable (i:nil) repeated AgreementInfo

                A download agreement (transfer type) and its cost. Requests: the agreements the user accepted (the client sends every type 1-7 in the file's list, omitting <cost> when it is 0). Responses: each FileEntry has 7 slots, one per client type in the order own, small, free, edu, access, transfer, points; the offered agreement sits at its type's position (Observed: own in slot 1, small in slot 2, transfer in slot 6; the other positions Inferred) and the other slots are nil. Exactly one agreement per file was offered in every live case.

                • <name> string required

                  Agreement (transfer type) name. The client knows a closed set (case-sensitive) and maps any other name to type 0, shown as "file(s) have been removed, moved to another folder or the folder password has been changed". Whether the server can send other names is Unknown, so the schema does not restrict the value.

                  NameClient typeMeaning (client texts)Cost unitLive
                  own1Your own file; free, without limits- (0)Observed: cost 0 for own files
                  small2File under 1 MB; free, not counted- (0)Observed: cost 0 for other users' files under 1 MB
                  free3The file owner pays the transfer-Not observed
                  edu4Chomik Edu file; free-Not observed (the programme appears discontinued)
                  access5Paid recently; free re-download for a few days-Not observed
                  transfer6Another user's file, charged to your transferkBObserved: 1654 for a 1,694,208-byte file (= floor(size / 1024))
                  points7Author file, paid with pointspointsNot observed
                  hdd8Client-internal: already on disk (also accepted from the server)-Never sent by the client
                  queued9Client-internal: already in the download queue (also accepted from the server)-Never sent by the client
                  mixed10Client UI state only (several types in one window), never a file's agreement--
                • <cost> integer (int32) optional

                  Cost of the agreement. Unit by type (client behaviour; consistent with the live values): transfer in kB (the client multiplies by 1024 for display; live, the transfer cost equalled the file size / 1024, rounded down), points in points. own and small were 0 live; the other free types are free per the client texts (server values Unknown). The client omits <cost> when it is 0, and a paid agreement (cost > 0) always opens its confirmation dialog.

Responses - 200, 500

200

SOAP response envelope. HTTP 200 is used for every service-level outcome, including errors: check DownloadResult/status. Compressed (Content-Encoding: gzip) when the request accepts gzip.

Schema text/xml

Schema DownloadResponseEnvelope, as an XML element tree in wire order. Namespaces are shown where they change.

  • <s:Envelope> object required DownloadResponseEnvelope xmlns http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

    SOAP 1.1 response envelope for Download: <s:Envelope><s:Body><DownloadResponse xmlns="http://chomikuj.pl/"><DownloadResult …>.

    • <s:Body> object required

      Exactly one response element; no other content.

      • <DownloadResponse> object required xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/
        • <DownloadResult> object required DownloadResult

          Result element; declares xmlns:i (XML Schema instance, for i:nil) and xmlns:a.

          • <a:status> string required Status xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Outcome of the call. The client accepts only Ok; BadToken triggers a re-login, anything else is an error.

            7 values
            • "Ok" Success. The only value the client treats as success.
            • "BadToken" Unknown, logged-out or otherwise invalid token. The client re-authenticates (Auth) once per message (message-relog-count=1) and resends the message with the new token; session-bound messages are dropped.
            • "Forbidden" Auth: user name does not exist. The client shows the credentials dialog.
            • "PermissionError" Auth: wrong password for an existing user. The client shows the credentials dialog.
            • "Error" Generic failure. Usually carries a reason in errorMessage (e.g. EmptyName, NameExistsAtDestination); FolderFiles with an unknown disposition returns Error with errorMessage nil (FolderFiles/invalid-disposition).
            • "NotEmptyOrNotExistsFolder" RemoveFolder with force=false on a folder that contains files, or on an unknown/removed folder id.
            • "WrongDisposition" FolderFiles: the disposition is a known value but not allowed for this call (download).
          • <a:errorMessage> string required nullable (i:nil) ErrorMessage xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Error detail for status=Error; nil otherwise.

          • <a:list> list optional nullable (i:nil) xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            File groups; empty for unknown ids and for a sequence whose entries span two folders; nil on error and for non-final sequence parts.

            • <DownloadFolder> object optional nullable (i:nil) repeated DownloadFolder xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

              A group of files from one folder in a Download result (DownloadFolder, parsed by).

              • <id> integer (int32) required

                Folder id.

              • <hamsterId> integer (int32) required

                Owner account id (another user's for other users' files).

              • <hamsterName> string optional

                Owner account name (redacted as {{OTHER_USER}} for other users).

              • <type> string optional

                Always empty in observations (own and other users' folders); not read by the client.

              • <name> string required

                Folder name.

              • <globalId> string optional

                Folder path /<user>/<folder>; with http://chomikuj.pl in front it is the folder's public web page (openPublicFolderPage, Observed). The client copies it into every file of the group and uses it only as a fallback id.

              • <files> list required

                Files of the group.

                • <FileEntry> object optional nullable (i:nil) repeated FileEntry

                  A file in a Download result.

                  • <id> integer (int64) required

                    File id. Entries with id <= 0 are skipped by the client.

                  • <agreementInfo> list optional

                    Offered (or accepted) agreements: always 7 slots, one per client type in the order own, small, free, edu, access, transfer, points; the offered agreement sits at its type's position (Observed: own 1, small 2, transfer 6) and the other slots are i:nil.

                    • <AgreementInfo> object optional nullable (i:nil) repeated AgreementInfo

                      A download agreement (transfer type) and its cost. Requests: the agreements the user accepted (the client sends every type 1-7 in the file's list, omitting <cost> when it is 0). Responses: each FileEntry has 7 slots, one per client type in the order own, small, free, edu, access, transfer, points; the offered agreement sits at its type's position (Observed: own in slot 1, small in slot 2, transfer in slot 6; the other positions Inferred) and the other slots are nil. Exactly one agreement per file was offered in every live case.

                      • <name> string required

                        Agreement (transfer type) name. The client knows a closed set (case-sensitive) and maps any other name to type 0, shown as "file(s) have been removed, moved to another folder or the folder password has been changed". Whether the server can send other names is Unknown, so the schema does not restrict the value.

                        NameClient typeMeaning (client texts)Cost unitLive
                        own1Your own file; free, without limits- (0)Observed: cost 0 for own files
                        small2File under 1 MB; free, not counted- (0)Observed: cost 0 for other users' files under 1 MB
                        free3The file owner pays the transfer-Not observed
                        edu4Chomik Edu file; free-Not observed (the programme appears discontinued)
                        access5Paid recently; free re-download for a few days-Not observed
                        transfer6Another user's file, charged to your transferkBObserved: 1654 for a 1,694,208-byte file (= floor(size / 1024))
                        points7Author file, paid with pointspointsNot observed
                        hdd8Client-internal: already on disk (also accepted from the server)-Never sent by the client
                        queued9Client-internal: already in the download queue (also accepted from the server)-Never sent by the client
                        mixed10Client UI state only (several types in one window), never a file's agreement--
                      • <cost> integer (int32) optional

                        Cost of the agreement. Unit by type (client behaviour; consistent with the live values): transfer in kB (the client multiplies by 1024 for display; live, the transfer cost equalled the file size / 1024, rounded down), points in points. own and small were 0 live; the other free types are free per the client texts (server values Unknown). The client omits <cost> when it is 0, and a paid agreement (cost > 0) always opens its confirmation dialog.

                  • <realId> integer (int64) optional nullable (i:nil)

                    Real (storage) id: nil for every file seen live, i.e. own uploads, playlist copies and other users' files. The client stores it and uses it only for entries without a file id (.<realId> form, playlists, queue). Meaning Inferred (the stored file shared by copies); when it is non-zero: Unknown.

                  • <name> string required

                    File name.

                  • <size> integer (int64) required

                    Approximate size in bytes (512-byte granularity: 100 B is reported as 512, 1033 B as 1536), not the exact length.

                  • <expire> string optional nullable (i:nil)

                    nil in every observation. The client does not read this member; only the expire of RefreshFileUrl is parsed.

                  • <url> string optional nullable (i:nil)

                    Signed download URL http://sNNNN.chomikuj.pl/File.aspx?e=..&pv=.. (see GET /File.aspx); nil until an agreement is accepted. Reusable for several GETs.

          • <a:accountBalance> object optional nullable (i:nil) AccountBalance xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Balance; nil on error and for non-final parts.

            • <transfer> object required nullable (i:nil) TransferBalance xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

              Transfer quota.

              • <value> integer (int64) required

                Remaining transfer in kB (the client shows it as MB after dividing by 1024; consistent with the live transfer agreement cost = size / 1024). Live value 51200 = 50 MB.

              • <limit> integer (int64) required

                Transfer limit in kB (live value 51200).

              • <extra> integer (int64) required

                Extra (purchased) transfer; presumably kB as well (Inferred).

            • <points> integer (int64) required xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

              Points balance.

          • <a:messageSequence> object optional nullable (i:nil) MessageSequence xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Echo of the request sequence; nil in the plain form.

            • <stamp> string required xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

              Random correlation value, the same for all parts (a random number generated by the client). The server does not key stored parts by it.

            • <part> integer (int32) required xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

              Zero-based part index.

            • <count> integer (int32) required xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

              Total number of parts.

Captured live on 2026-10-24T15:26:40Z: HTTP 200 OK, Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8, Content-Encoding: gzip (368 bytes on the wire, 468 decoded; the example shows the decoded body).

MessageSequence part 0 of count 2 (the client splits >2000 entries into chunks). Observed: status Ok but list and accountBalance are nil and only messageSequence is echoed - the server acknowledges non-final parts. Only part 0 was sent in this run; the follow-up (sequence-*, seq1c-*, seq1d-*) showed what a final part returns: the stored and its own entries if they are in one folder, Ok with an empty list across folders, Error when nothing is stored in the session.

Evidence level: the acknowledgement of the non-final part is Observed here; the behaviour of the final part was verified live in the follow-up.

Client vs live - discrepancies

Where the client's expected behaviour and the live service disagree, the spec follows the live behaviour (x-discrepancies):

  • sequence is optional: the client sends the sequenced form only when configured, and both forms work.
  • The client id form <hamsterId>/<folderId>, built by its "download folder" action, triggers an unhandled server exception (a:InternalServiceFault); a folder path works.
  • DownloadFolder has an extra type member and FileEntry an extra expire member; the client reads neither.
  • Final part of a sequence: the client expects it to return the data; live it does, with conditions (per-session store, Error without a stored part, empty list across folders, agreements from the final message only).
  • Agreement slots: the offered agreement is not always the first slot; for other users' files small is in slot 2 and transfer in slot 6. The client keeps only named entries in server order, so its main type is unaffected.

Security notes - findings that concern Download

  • S-06 Low Out-of-order or wrong-namespace parameters are silently dropped (null/0); some malformed requests (operation element without the trailing slash, the hamsterId/folderId Download id, an empty Auth) trigger an unhandled a:InternalServiceFault. The client's own "download folder" action builds exactly that hamsterId/folderId id, so that feature presumably fails against today's server (Inferred).
  • S-08 Low Signed File.aspx?e=…&pv=… download URLs are reusable bearer URLs (repeat GET and Range work); expire was always empty, so their lifetime is unknown.
  • S-13 Low (correctness) Sequenced-Download state is per session, not per request: stored parts are keyed by the session token (not the stamp), are not cleared by a final part, and a stale part from another folder makes a later final part silently return an empty list (status Ok). Clients that reuse a session can get wrong or empty results.

From x-security-notes in the spec. Ratings and scope are explained on Security & privacy.
